subject: AI & Agents
title: Next-Token Prediction
description: A quick win: understand Next-Token Prediction.

hook.text: Your phone suggests the next word as you type. Large language models do the same — at massive scale.

buildup.text: Given a sequence of words, the model predicts the most probable next one.

discovery.text: Repeat this billions of times on internet text and the model learns grammar, facts, and style.

twist.text: It doesn't 'know' anything. It just got extremely good at finishing sentences.

climax.text: ChatGPT writes essays, code, and poetry — all from next-token prediction.

quiz.question: What is the core task behind large language models?
options: Predicting the next token in a sequence
Translating all text to English first

details.summary: Large language models work by predicting the most likely next token given all previous tokens. This simple mechanism — repeated billions of times during training — produces the sophisticated language abilities of modern AI.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding next-token prediction reveals the elegance and limitation of LLMs. Their impressive outputs emerge from prediction, not understanding, which explains both their power and their failures.
takeaways: LLMs predict the most probable next word or token
This simple mechanism produces sophisticated language output
Prediction without understanding explains hallucinations and errors

faq.question: If LLMs just predict the next word, how can they reason?
faq.answer: Training on vast text that contains reasoning examples teaches the model to produce reasoning-like sequences. Whether this constitutes genuine reasoning or sophisticated pattern matching is actively debated.

faq.question: Why does next-token prediction sometimes produce nonsense?
faq.answer: The model predicts what text is statistically likely, not what is true. Plausible-sounding false statements are statistically similar to true ones. The model has no mechanism to verify factual accuracy.
